visible.title: Setting STREAMLIT_CLIENT_TOOLBAR_MODE environment variable does not work
visible.body:
### Checklist

### Summary

I'm trying to set the toolbar mode for my streamlit app using the environment variable:
`STREAMLIT_CLIENT_TOOLBAR_MODE=viewer` 
However, this seems to have no effect and the toolbar is still visible. I have not used a command line flag for this variable, and so the environment variable should take precedent according to the following code:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/49277083064190c732c0551157be6fb6c437fdcc/lib/streamlit/config.py#L1221

For the environment variable, I followed the syntax outlined in the [Streamlit Docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/configuration) (point 3)

### Reproducible Code Example

### Steps To Reproduce

### Expected Behavior

Toolbar disappears

### Current Behavior

Toolbar still present

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.28.2
- Python version: 3.10.12
- Operating System: Ubuntu
- Browser: Safari

### Additional Information

gold.summary: STREAMLIT_CLIENT_TOOLBAR_MODE=viewer seems to have no effect (toolbar still visible).
hypotheses: expected: 'viewer' hides only developer options; 'minimal' hides more
acceptable_next_steps: Explain viewer versus minimal and test minimal if hiding the menu is the goal.
Inspect the effective client.toolbarMode if developer controls specifically remain exposed.
must_not: Promise minimal removes every toolbar/control in every context.
gold.reference: Maintainer: viewer only hides developer options, working as expected; use minimal.
gold.review_reason: Keeping a toolbar visible is consistent with viewer hiding developer options rather than the entire menu. Explain minimal versus viewer; do not infer the environment variable failed merely from visibility.

acceptable_next_steps: Explain the difference between viewer and minimal using the config docs; suggest minimal
must_not: claim env vars are not supported
